capabilities: Run Claude Code sessions as terminal tabs inside the vault
Show a dashboard with usage limits, context size and vault status
Combine briefing points, macOS reminders and tasks in a today card
Continue projects from the handoff note of an earlier session
Block excluded vault files from Claude sessions, optionally via sandbox
disambiguation: Not only a dashboard; its core job is running Claude Code sessions as terminal tabs, and the cockpit picture is one view of the status data.
extras: Settings and labels are German only. macOS on Apple Silicon is the tested platform; Windows lacks the status line, limits and sandbox. The permission-skip switch starts sessions with --dangerously-skip-permissions, which the README explicitly warns about. The node-pty binary is downloaded separately and verified against built-in SHA256 checksums; releases carry GitHub attestations. The README includes extensive disclosures about programs run, files read and written, and network access, and states there is no telemetry.
intentEvidence: inspired by the Agentic OS plugin from skaile.de and is an independent rebuild with its own code
motivation: The author was inspired by the Agentic OS plugin from skaile.de and built an independent rebuild with its own code.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to run, monitor or hand off Claude Code agent sessions from inside the app.
